problem: Open-vocabulary visual-language maps merge multi-view 2D masks using only proximity or structural overlap, so incomplete point clouds and occlusion cause wrong merges. Their instruction grounding also stays tied to predefined object lexicons, so fine-grained, context-dependent instructions are grounded poorly.
motivation: Grounding free-form instructions to specific 3D instances is needed for instruction-driven navigation, yet map-based grounding often underperforms even basic VLM text-to-image matching. The authors observe that CLIP-style features separate spatially adjacent but distinct instances, so semantics can complement geometry in merging. They also observe that LLMs are limited by fixed vocabularies and do not use spatial context around candidates.
key_idea: Merge 2D masks into 3D instances only when both a structural containment consensus and a vision-language similarity agree, then let an LLM parse instructions into free-form descriptions and pick among candidates using nearby-object context.
insight: Structure and semantics are complementary. The mapping ablation shows structure-only gives AP 12.2, semantics-only (with OVIR-3D's local structure) gives 10.1, and both give 14.3. In grounding, free-form parsing contributes more than context-based selection: removing parsing lowers SR from 49.6 to 44.7, removing selection lowers it to 47.2, and removing both gives 38.1. Hyperparameters (τ_thres 0.5–0.7, N_c 4–12) change results only slightly.
method: Structural consensus rate: back-project each mask to 3D and find the frames observing both masks (observers). Supporters are frames where a larger mask contains both masks (τ_sub=0.8). R_struc is |supporters|/|observers|.
Semantic similarity rate: cosine similarity of OVSAM mask features. Two masks merge if R_struc*R_seman >= τ_thres (0.6).

Iterative mask merging: follows MaskClustering. Pairs with more observers merge first, using a decreasing observer-count threshold N_o (top 5% of pairs, reduced by 5% per iteration). Consensus rates are recomputed after each merge using the most complete mask's features.

Instance feature aggregation: as in OpenMask3D, take the top-k covering masks with L multi-level crops and average CLIP ViT-H features. 2D masks come from CropFormer, plus MaskClustering post-processing.

Generic instruction parsing: GPT-4 converts an instruction into a short, free-form, fine-grained instance description (not a fixed vocabulary). The top N_c=8 map instances are retrieved by CLIP similarity.

Context-aware instance selection: for each candidate, a KD-tree finds the N_s=5 nearest instances within 2 m, which are labeled with LVIS. A second LLM round chooses the target in a multiple-choice format from locations, similarities and neighbors.

setting.backbone: CropFormer (2D masks) + OVSAM (consensus features) + CLIP ViT-H (instance features) + GPT-4 (frozen, instruction grounding)
setting.training_data: none (training-free / zero-shot; uses off-the-shelf pretrained models)
setting.observation: multi-view posed RGB-D sequences used to build a 3D map (full scene mapping before querying)
setting.action_space: none (offline instruction-to-instance retrieval, not navigation control)
setting.simulator: none (ScanNet200 scans; Matterport3D semantics scenes with Habitat-derived data)
setting.privileged: none for the method beyond RGB-D and poses; full-scene mapping is done before querying

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 Matterport3D scenes (11 from R2R-CE val-unseen, 9 from the VLMap evaluation set), with instructions drawn from R2R-CE, VLMap and ALFRED
numbers.extra: Full-scene mapping first; success = target retrieved within 1 m of the GT center; SR_k = success within k retrieval attempts

numbers_note: The benchmarks are not standard navigation benchmarks; the Matterport3D retrieval set is a custom 20-scene subset. The hyperparameter table reports mean ± spread over ranges, and these are not included.
results: On ScanNet200, OpenMap is the best fully zero-shot method with AP 14.3, AP50 26.0 and AP25 33.3, beating MaskClustering (12.0, 23.3, 30.1) and OVIR-3D. On Matterport3D target retrieval with GPT-4, it reaches SR 49.6 versus 40.9 for ConceptGraphs, 27.2 for VLMap and 25.1 for NLMap, and SR16 of 73.7 versus 54.9 for ConceptGraphs.
limitations: Evaluation is offline mapping and target retrieval on a custom 20-scene Matterport3D subset. There is no closed-loop navigation, no standard VLN or ObjectNav benchmark, and no real-robot test.
Requires full-scene RGB-D mapping and poses beforehand, and depends on the quality of CropFormer, OVSAM and CLIP. CLIP's limited text length forces short descriptions.
Fixed LVIS labels are still used for neighbor objects in the selection step, and the system relies on GPT-4 (closed).
